topic: Visual and sensor realism, Real2Sim, and neural/generative realism for AICHEMIST's general-purpose digital twin platform (status as of 2026-10-06)
executive_summary: Recommendation: do not build a renderer. Build on the NVIDIA OpenUSD/Omniverse RTX stack. Isaac Sim 6.0 went GA in June 2026 and 6.1.0 is out (Sep 2026). Isaac Sim now renders 3D Gaussian splats (3DGS/3DGUT) via the Fabric Scene Delegate, with multi-GPU, light interaction with meshes and MaterialX. Splats are stored in the new OpenUSD 26.03 UsdVolParticleField3DGaussianSplat schema. Real-time path tracing (RTX Real-Time 2.0) is the default render mode, and RTX lidar/radar/ultrasonic sensors sit in the same scene. The neural-reconstruction core has converged on permissively licensed NVIDIA/Berkeley code: gsplat (Apache-2.0, v1.6.0; 3DGUT, spinning-lidar rasterization, NCore v4, multi-GPU) and 3DGRUT (Apache-2.0, v1.1.0 on 2026-06-10, v2.0.0 with Neural Harmonic Textures in June 2026). Both handle fisheye/rolling-shutter cameras, include a physically-plausible ISP, and export NuRec USDZ for Isaac Sim, AlpaSim (Apache-2.0, ~900 reconstructed AV scenes) and CARLA. NeRF is no longer competitive as a simulation runtime: 3DGS/3DGUT is 100-200x faster to render and is now standardized (OpenUSD ParticleField, Khronos KHR_gaussian_splatting RC Feb 2026). NeRF survives only as a niche offline/extrapolation tool. CEN's NeRF-based 2D->3D pipeline should therefore be migrated, and its license checked (Instant-NGP is Nvidia Source Code License-NC). The biggest hidden risk is licensing. The original Inria 3DGS code and most mesh-extraction research code are non-commercial: 2DGS and MILo (Gaussian-Splatting License), PGSR (ZJU non-profit), and Neuralangelo, Instant-NGP and nvdiffrast (NVIDIA NC). TRELLIS.2 is MIT but depends on nvdiffrast. Tencent's Hunyuan3D 2.1 license explicitly excludes South Korea, the EU and the UK, so a Korean company cannot legally use it. Commercially usable building blocks exist and should form the default stack: gsplat, 3DGRUT, fVDB Reality Capture, TRELLIS/TRELLIS.2 (MIT, minus nvdiffrast), SAM 3D Objects (SAM License), VGGT-1B-Commercial, MapAnything-apache, Depth Anything 3 small/base/metric (Apache), CoACD/CuACD (MIT), Articulate-Anything (MIT), Cosmos 3 (OpenMDW-1.1) and Cosmos Transfer 2.5 (NVIDIA Open Model License). Generative world models are now credible tools for appearance-level sim-to-real augmentation and policy evaluation, but they cannot replace physics. Examples: Cosmos Transfer 2.5 (depth/edge/blur/segmentation multi-ControlNet, distilled edge model Feb 2026), Cosmos 3 (omnimodel, May/June 2026), Wayve GAIA-3/4, Runway GWM-1 Robotics, Decart Oasis 3 ($0.02/s API) and Genie 3 (consumer prototype only, no API). Use them as a post-render domain-adaptation layer with label-preserving controls and as an evaluation oracle. Physics, ground-truth labels and sensors stay in the simulator. The strategic move for CEN is to turn 'NeRF photo->3D' into a Real2Sim Asset Factory. The pipeline: phone/robot video -> feed-forward poses/depth -> 3DGUT splat (visual) -> surface mesh plus generative completion -> part segmentation and articulation (URDF/MJCF/USD Physics) -> convex decomposition -> VLM priors for mass/friction refined by video system identification -> automated physics validation -> a SimReady USD with a measured 'sim2real certificate'. This product, sold through the existing marketplace together with Korea-specific captured environments (factories, logistics, Korean roads), is a defensible moat because NVIDIA supplies tools but not curated, validated, domain-specific sim-ready content. Gap measurement must be built in from day 1. FID alone does not predict detector mAP, while newer structure-plus-appearance metrics reach Pearson r≈0.87-0.88 with downstream mAP, and splat-based real-to-sim policy evaluation (PolaRiS, soft-body GS twins) shows strong sim/real success-rate correlation. CEN should ship a Sim2Real Gap Scorecard covering perception mAP-transfer ratio, policy success correlation, physical trajectory error and sensor statistics as a platform feature. Note: the session's web-search budget ran out after ~60 searches. Later verification used primary GitHub sources. Items marked low confidence below were not verifiable with the remaining tools.

options.name: NVIDIA Omniverse RTX Renderer inside Isaac Sim 6.x (RTX Real-Time 2.0 + Interactive Path Tracing)
options.status_as_of_2026: Isaac Sim 6.0 GA ~June 2026 (radiancefields report: June 8, 2026; GitHub tag v6.0.0 June 4), 6.0.1 (June 22), 6.1.0 GA (Sep 10, 2026), 7.0.0a1 pre-release (Sep 18, 2026). The fetch tool printed some GitHub tag years inconsistently, but the sequence matches 2026. RTX Real-Time 2.0 is a path-tracing-based real-time mode using the DLSS suite; Interactive (Path Tracing) mode is available for higher fidelity. Isaac Sim 6.0 adds 3DGS rendering via Fabric Scene Delegate, multi-GPU, light interaction with mesh scenes, and MaterialX.
options.license_and_cost: Isaac Sim source on GitHub is Apache-2.0, but Omniverse Kit/RTX runtime requires accepting the NVIDIA Omniverse License Terms on first launch. Free to use; commercial SaaS redistribution should be confirmed with NVIDIA. Needs RT-core GPUs: datacenter minimum A40, recommended L40S, best RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server. H100/A100 are not on the list.
strengths: Physically based path tracing with MDL + MaterialX/OpenPBR materials, fully OpenUSD-native
Same scene hosts RTX camera, lidar, radar and acoustic/ultrasonic sensors (isaacsim.sensors.experimental.rtx)
Native Gaussian-splat (NuRec/3DGUT) rendering composited with meshes, and lighting interaction since 6.0
Direct coupling to Isaac Lab 3.0 (RL/IL), Newton/PhysX physics, Cosmos augmentation, Replicator domain randomization
Largest robotics ecosystem; NVIDIA is shipping the Real2Sim tooling (NuRec, 3DGRUT, gsplat 3DGUT) into it
weaknesses: Vendor lock-in to NVIDIA RTX GPUs and the Omniverse license
Heavy (Kit) runtime; Isaac Lab 3.0 adds kit-less OVRTX/Newton renderers partly to work around this
Splats still need proxy meshes for physics; lidar/radar on splat content is less mature than on meshes (gsplat added lidar rasterization separately)
Fast API churn (e.g., isaacsim.sensors.rtx deprecated for experimental.rtx in 6.0)
options.best_fit: Default rendering + sensor + Real2Sim runtime for robots, factories/warehouses, drones and the core of CEN's GPU workspace

options.name: Isaac Lab 3.0 rendering backends (Isaac RTX, OVRTX kit-less, Newton Warp renderer, Newton GL/RTX) + physically-plausible ISP
options.status_as_of_2026: Isaac Lab 3.0 beta at GTC (Mar 17, 2026), beta2 (Jun 17, 2026), 3.0.0-EA (Sep 16, 2026). Built on Newton 1.0 + PhysX, with kit-less Newton backend (MuJoCo-Warp solvers), pluggable visualizers (Kit, Newton, Rerun, Viser), a renderer-neutral physically plausible ISP (HDR->LDR) and a visuo-tactile sensor (TacSL).
options.license_and_cost: Isaac Lab is BSD-3/Apache-style open source. The Isaac RTX backend inherits Omniverse terms. cuRobo-based SkillGen has proprietary terms.
strengths: Massively parallel tiled camera rendering for vision-based RL
Choice of cheap raster (Newton Warp) vs full RTX per experiment
ISP model shared across renderers reduces camera-appearance gap
weaknesses: Early-access APIs
TacSL tactile works only with the PhysX backend, not Newton
Kit-less renderers are lower fidelity than full RTX
options.best_fit: CEN 'train' tab: vision-based RL/IL at scale with switchable fidelity

options.name: Unreal Engine 5.7 / 5.8 (Lumen, Nanite, MegaLights, Substrate), incl. CARLA
options.status_as_of_2026: UE 5.7 (Nov 2025): MegaLights Beta, Substrate Production-Ready, Nanite Foliage (Nanite Voxels) Experimental, PCG Production-Ready. UE 5.8 (June 17, 2026): Lumen Lite (~2x faster GI), MegaLights/Movie Render Graph production-ready, Mesh Terrain. 5.8 is the last UE5. UE6 early access targeted by late 2027. 3DGS via third-party plugins (YaGS open source, UE 5.5-5.7; NanoGS; Volinga 4DGS relighting). CARLA integrates NuRec.
options.license_and_cost: Source-available EULA. Royalty/seat model for non-game commercial use. Exact 2026 terms not verified in this session (low confidence).
strengths: Best-in-class real-time artist-driven visuals, huge environment marketplace
Strong for AV/off-road/large open worlds (PCG, Nanite foliage)
CARLA ecosystem for driving
weaknesses: Not physically based for sensors (raster/Lumen approximations), weak robotics physics/articulation
No native USD-physics/Isaac Lab-grade RL tooling
UE6 transition in 2027 means engine-level rework risk
Splat support only via plugins
options.best_fit: Optional AV/driving and visualization front-end when customers already use UE/CARLA. Not the core.

options.name: Unity 6 HDRP
options.status_as_of_2026: Unity's 2026 render-pipeline strategy puts HDRP in maintenance (no new features, stability fixes only) and prioritizes URP. Built-in pipeline deprecation starts in 6.5. A unified renderer is a long-term goal only. Splats via XGRIDS LCC Unity SDK 2.2.0 (real-time lights + shadows on splats).
options.license_and_cost: Unity Pro/Industry subscription (per-seat).
strengths: Large dev community, good XR/mobile deployment
Third-party splat SDKs with lighting
weaknesses: HDRP is frozen, so the photoreal path has no roadmap
Weak robotics physics/sensor ecosystem compared with Isaac
options.best_fit: Avoid for new high-fidelity simulation. Acceptable only for XR/mobile viewers.

options.name: Blender 5.x Cycles / EEVEE (with BlenderProc-style SDG)
options.status_as_of_2026: Blender 5.0 (Nov 2025): ACES 1.3/2.0, null-scattering volumes, thin-film. Blender 5.1 (Mar 11, 2026): up to 10% faster GPU Cycles, HIP RT default on AMD.
options.license_and_cost: GPL (free). Rendered outputs are unrestricted.
strengths: Ground-truth-quality path tracing that runs on any CUDA/OptiX/HIP GPU, including non-RT H100s via CUDA
Excellent for offline image dataset generation (CEN's current core) and asset cleanup/retopology
Scriptable, huge asset community
weaknesses: Not real-time and no robotics physics loop
GPL constraints if code is linked/distributed
options.best_fit: Offline photoreal dataset rendering and the asset-cleanup step in the Real2Sim factory

options.name: Godot 4.5/4.6/4.7
options.status_as_of_2026: 4.5 (Sep 2025) and 4.6 (Jan 2026: Jolt physics default, SSR rewrite). 4.7 beta (Apr 2026) adds HDR output and Vulkan ray-tracing work.
options.license_and_cost: MIT, free
strengths: Fully permissive, lightweight, embeddable (LibGodot)
weaknesses: SDFGI/raster GI far below path-traced realism
No sensor-grade simulation or robotics ecosystem
options.best_fit: Not recommended for realism. Possibly lightweight embedded viewers.

options.name: WebGPU web renderers (PlayCanvas engine + SuperSplat 3.0, World Labs Spark 2.x, Babylon.js, CesiumJS)
options.status_as_of_2026: WebGPU on by default in Chrome, Edge, Firefox (Windows Jul 2025, macOS Nov 2025) and Safari 26 (Sep 2025, incl. iOS/visionOS). SuperSplat 3.0 (June 3, 2026) is WebGPU-only and streams 24M-Gaussian scans at ~60 fps with LOD. Spark 2.x (World Labs, MIT, WebGL2, LoD paging for 100M+ splat worlds). KHR_gaussian_splatting shipped in Cesium, Babylon.js and PlayCanvas.
options.license_and_cost: PlayCanvas engine MIT, Spark MIT. Free.
strengths: Zero-install previews for CEN marketplace and browser workspace
Splat streaming at world scale on mobile/VR
Standards-based (glTF KHR_gaussian_splatting, SPZ)
weaknesses: No physically based sensor simulation and no ground-truth labels at sensor fidelity
Browser GPU limits
options.best_fit: CEN marketplace asset/scene previews, lightweight annotation/editing, sharing digital-twin views. Heavy simulation stays server-side (Omniverse streaming).

options.name: gsplat (nerfstudio-project)
options.status_as_of_2026: v1.6.0 on main (not yet on PyPI). 3DGUT integration (Apr 2025), external distortion + lidar rasterization (Mar 2026), NCore v4 (Apr 2026), fisheye/FTheta/lidar camera models and ~30% faster MCMC (Jun 2026), multi-GPU + PPISP (Jul 2026), SH optimizations (Aug 2026). 5.8k stars.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free
strengths: Commercial-safe replacement for the Inria non-commercial code
Up to 4x less GPU memory and 15% less time than the official implementation
Rolling-shutter/distortion (3DGUT), lidar, batching across scenes, 2DGS mode
Used by NVIDIA NuRec as renderer
weaknesses: Library only: needs our own pipeline, UI and QA
No built-in physics/collision geometry
options.best_fit: Core reconstruction engine of the CEN Real2Sim factory

options.name: NVIDIA 3DGRUT (3DGRT ray-traced + 3DGUT unscented-transform splats)
options.status_as_of_2026: v1.0.0 (Apr 3, 2025), PPISP (Jan 2026), NCore v4 (Mar 2026), v1.1.0 (Jun 10, 2026: USD/USDZ/PLY/NuRec export with mesh injection, path-traced playground, Blackwell/CUDA 13, DGX Spark), v2.0.0 (Jun 2026: Neural Harmonic Textures). 3DGUT was a CVPR 2025 oral; 3DGRT was SIGGRAPH Asia 2024.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0, free. Needs RT-core GPU for 3DGRT.
strengths: Handles distorted, fisheye and rolling-shutter cameras, which matters for robots/AVs
Secondary rays (reflections/refractions, shadows) via ray tracing
Direct export to Isaac Sim / NuRec USDZ and OpenUSD ParticleField
RTX 5090: 3DGUT 846 FPS (NeRF-Synthetic), 317 FPS (MipNeRF360)
weaknesses: Research-grade tooling
3DGRT slower (68 FPS on MipNeRF360)
options.best_fit: High-fidelity sensor-correct scene reconstruction for robot/AV digital twins

options.name: Omniverse NuRec + AlpaSim (+CARLA integration)
options.status_as_of_2026: NuRec is a set of 3DGS libraries that reconstruct camera/lidar data into OpenUSD and render via gsplat inside Isaac Sim, AlpaSim and CARLA (announced Aug 2025). AlpaSim is open source (Apache-2.0, Oct 2025), runs as gRPC microservices, uses NuRec 3DGUT as default renderer (plus OmniDreams video-model rendering), ships PhysicalAI-AV-NuRec 26.01 dataset (~900 x 20 s long-tail scenes) and reports up to 83% variance reduction in real-world metrics.
options.license_and_cost: AlpaSim Apache-2.0. NuRec container/library terms not verified (docs.nvidia.com blocked): low confidence.
strengths: Production path from capture to closed-loop sim
AV-ready (multi-camera, lidar, trajectories)
Standardized on OpenUSD ParticleField
weaknesses: Reconstructed scenes are mostly static and limited in novel-trajectory extrapolation
Actors/dynamic objects need insertion and relighting
NVIDIA-centric
options.best_fit: Driving digital twins and site-specific robot test environments

options.name: fVDB Reality Capture (NVIDIA / OpenVDB)
options.status_as_of_2026: Active (fVDB 0.4 around GTC 2026). Toolbox for sensor loading, radiance-field reconstruction, feature learning, mesh/point-cloud extraction, USD export.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0
strengths: Claims ~50% better end-to-end throughput than gsplat and 30% lower runtime
Commercial-safe mesh extraction path
Sparse VDB scales to large sites
weaknesses: Small community (69 stars)
Young API
options.best_fit: Factory/warehouse-scale capture and commercial-safe mesh extraction

options.name: NeRF ecosystem (nerfstudio/nerfacto, Instant-NGP, Zip-NeRF)
options.status_as_of_2026: nerfstudio is active (Apache-2.0, 12k stars, splatfacto uses gsplat). Instant-NGP is effectively legacy. Zip-NeRF is high quality but takes seconds per frame. Isaac Sim can still render NeRF USDZ.
options.license_and_cost: nerfstudio Apache-2.0. Instant-NGP under Nvidia Source Code License-NC (non-commercial; commercial requires NVIDIA research licensing).
strengths: Better extrapolation to views far from training cameras
Compact neural fields, good for offline novel-view data
weaknesses: 100-200x slower rendering than 3DGS; not real-time for multi-sensor RL
Not standardized in USD/glTF like splats; ecosystem momentum has moved to 3DGS
Instant-NGP licensing blocks commercial use
options.best_fit: Keep only as an offline fallback. Migrate CEN's NeRF pipeline to 3DGUT/gsplat.

options.name: Splat-to-mesh / surface reconstruction for collision (2DGS, PGSR, SuGaR, MILo, Neuralangelo, AnyGS2Mesh)
options.status_as_of_2026: 2DGS (SIGGRAPH 2024), PGSR (TVCG; ~1 h on 1 GPU vs NeRF-SDF 8 GPUs x 2 days), MILo (SIGGRAPH Asia 2025, order of magnitude fewer vertices, 250K-14M configurable), Neuralangelo (CVPR 2023). Feed-forward GS-to-mesh appearing (AnyGS2Mesh, arXiv 2609.03304).
options.license_and_cost: 2DGS and MILo: Gaussian-Splatting License (Inria, research/evaluation only). PGSR: ZJU license, 'educational, research and non-profit purposes only'. Neuralangelo: NVIDIA research license (business via licensing form). SuGaR: likely Inria-derived (not verified; low confidence). Commercial-safe alternatives: gsplat 2DGS mode, fVDB, own re-implementation from papers.
strengths: Watertight-ish surfaces suitable for convex decomposition / SDF collision
Planar priors (PGSR) good for indoor/industrial
weaknesses: Almost all reference code is non-commercial
Thin structures, transparent/reflective surfaces still fail
Meshes need retopology/simplification before physics
options.best_fit: Re-implement the best ideas (2DGS/PGSR/MILo) on Apache gsplat/fVDB inside CEN

options.name: Physics-aware splats & real-to-sim evaluation (PhysGaussian, PhysTwin, OmniPhysGS, soft-body GS eval, PolaRiS, SplatSim)
options.status_as_of_2026: PhysGaussian (CVPR 2024 Highlight; MPM via warp-mpm, no meshing). PhysTwin (ICCV 2025; spring-mass + GS from sparse videos; ropes, cloth, plush, packages). OmniPhysGS (2025, constitutive Gaussians). Real-to-Sim soft-body GS policy evaluation (arXiv 2511.04665; ACT/DP/pi0/SmolVLA sim-real correlation). PolaRiS (arXiv 2512.16881; short video -> GS eval env with strong real correlation and co-training recipe). SplatSim (86.25% zero-shot real success vs 97.5% real-data-trained).
options.license_and_cost: Mostly academic code with varying licenses (verify individually; PhysGaussian license not stated on repo page).
strengths: Closes visual gap and deformable-physics gap together
Proven value for policy evaluation (sim success predicts real success)
weaknesses: Per-object/scene optimization, not yet general
MPM/spring-mass parameters are object-specific; slow for large-scale RL
options.best_fit: Phase-3 'deformables + evaluation twin' feature; the PolaRiS-style evaluation hub is a strong product template for CEN

options.name: Feed-forward 3D foundation models (VGGT, MapAnything, Depth Anything 3, AnySplat)
options.status_as_of_2026: VGGT (CVPR 2025 Best Paper; commercial checkpoint Jul 29, 2025; VGGT-Omega May 18, 2026). MapAnything (Sep 2025, 3DV 2026; metric multi-modal inputs). Depth Anything 3 (Nov 14, 2025; outperforms VGGT on pose/geometry; any-view feed-forward 3DGS).
options.license_and_cost: VGGT-1B-Commercial: commercial OK (application form; no military). VGGT-1B: non-commercial. MapAnything: code Apache-2.0; weights 'map-anything-apache' Apache-2.0 vs default CC-BY-NC. DA3: Small/Base/Metric-Large/Mono-Large Apache-2.0; Large/Giant/Nested CC-BY-NC-4.0.
strengths: Replaces slow/fragile COLMAP for consumer captures
Metric scale (MapAnything, DA3-Metric), which is essential for physics-correct assets
Seconds instead of hours
weaknesses: Best-quality weights are often NC
Accuracy still below calibrated SfM for large sites
options.best_fit: Front end of CEN capture pipeline (phone video -> poses, metric depth -> splat init)

options.name: Microsoft TRELLIS / TRELLIS.2-4B
options.status_as_of_2026: TRELLIS.2-4B released ~Dec 2025: O-Voxel sparse structure + flow-matching transformers, full PBR (base color, roughness, metallic, opacity). H100 timings: 512³ ~3 s, 1024³ ~17 s, 1536³ ~60 s. Needs ≥24 GB GPU. Full training code (Objaverse-XL).
options.license_and_cost: MIT (code and weights). However, dependencies nvdiffrast (Nvidia Source Code License, 1-way commercial: non-commercial only) and nvdiffrec have separate licenses. These must be replaced or licensed for commercial use.
strengths: Best permissively licensed open generator; trainable on our own data
Handles open surfaces/non-manifold and internal structure
PBR output useful for RTX rendering
weaknesses: Outputs are not watertight/simulation-ready and have no scale, mass or articulation
nvdiffrast dependency is a commercial-license trap
options.best_fit: Shape/texture completion of occluded parts in the Real2Sim factory and a text/image-to-asset generator in CEN

options.name: Tencent Hunyuan3D 2.1 (open) / 2.5-3.1 (API)
options.status_as_of_2026: 2.1 open-sourced Jun 13, 2025 with PBR texture; VRAM 10 GB shape, 21 GB texture, 29 GB combined. 2.5/3.0/3.1 Pro are closed (Tencent Cloud API, global English API from Nov 25, 2025; 3.0 = 1536³ geometry).
options.license_and_cost: Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.1 Community License. Territory = worldwide EXCLUDING the EU, UK and SOUTH KOREA; use of outputs outside the Territory is unlicensed; plus a >1M MAU approval clause. A Korean company cannot legally use the open weights. API terms for Korea not verified.
strengths: Strong quality, good PBR
weaknesses: License explicitly excludes South Korea: disqualifying for AICHEMIST
Newer versions closed
options.best_fit: Do NOT use (benchmark reference only, done by a non-Korean entity if at all)

options.name: Meta SAM 3D Objects
options.status_as_of_2026: Released Nov 19, 2025 with SAM 3. Predicts geometry, texture and layout/pose of a prompted object (mask/point/box) from one image, outputting Gaussian splats (.ply) and meshes. Encoder weights Jun 1, 2026; 3D Artist Object Set + HF leaderboard Jun 2, 2026. Companion SAM 3D Body.
options.license_and_cost: SAM License (custom): royalty-free and worldwide, commercial use allowed with restrictions (e.g., military). Medium confidence on full terms.
strengths: Works on cluttered in-the-wild photos with occlusion, outputs object pose/layout (scene-consistent)
Pairs naturally with SAM 3 segmentation for scene decomposition
weaknesses: Single-view hallucination; scale ambiguous
No physics/articulation
options.best_fit: Object instancing from a single photo of a real scene (Real2Sim of clutter), complementary to multi-view splats

options.name: Stability SPAR3D
options.status_as_of_2026: Point-cloud-conditioned editing then mesh in ~0.3 s (2025). No notable 2026 update found.
options.license_and_cost: Stability AI Community License: free for orgs <$1M annual revenue; enterprise license above that.
strengths: Very fast, editable point cloud stage
weaknesses: Lower quality than TRELLIS.2; revenue-capped license
options.best_fit: Low priority; interactive preview only

options.name: Commercial 3D generators (Meshy 6, Tripo 3.0, Rodin Gen-2.5)
options.status_as_of_2026: Meshy 6 (Pro $20/mo, Max $60/mo, Enterprise/API ~$90/mo; free outputs CC BY 4.0 non-commercial). Tripo 3.0 (Ultra up to 2M polys; Pro $12/mo; commercial rights all tiers). Rodin Gen-2.5 (Nov 2025; ~$0.50-1.50 per model).
options.license_and_cost: Paid tiers grant commercial rights; per-asset costs as listed (medium confidence, aggregator sources).
strengths: Fast, polished, game-ready topology
weaknesses: Not sim-ready (no mass/collision/articulation); vendor dependency; competitors to CEN's own generator
options.best_fit: Benchmark baselines and optional marketplace import connectors

options.name: World Labs Marble (+ World API)
options.status_as_of_2026: Beta Sep 2025, GA Nov 12, 2025, World API Jan 2026, Marble 1.1 Apr 2026. Outputs Gaussian splats (SPZ/PLY 2M/500K), collider GLB mesh, HQ GLB mesh, 360 panos. Export to Unreal, Unity, Blender, Houdini.
options.license_and_cost: Free tier cannot export. Standard plan exports splats + collider meshes. Pro plan required for HQ mesh and commercial rights. API from ~$0.12 per Draft world (medium confidence).
strengths: Only commercial generator that outputs splat + collider mesh = near sim-ready environments
Spark renderer (MIT) for web
weaknesses: Closed model; physics-agnostic beyond collider; scale/semantics not guaranteed
options.best_fit: Long-tail environment generation for CEN scenes (backgrounds) via API; also a competitive threat

options.name: Sim-ready conversion toolchain (CoACD/CuACD, V-HACD, PhysX-Anything, Articulate-Anything, Real2Code, URDFormer, ManiTwin, SLAT-Phys, Phys2Real)
options.status_as_of_2026: CoACD (SIGGRAPH 2022; MIT) with new GPU CuACD (Sep 2026, ~100x faster, ~0.25 s/mesh on RTX 4090). PhysX-Anything (CVPR 2026; Qwen2.5-VL; single image -> URDF/MJCF with mass, friction, joints; tested in MuJoCo; deformables unstable). Articulate-Anything (ICLR 2025; MIT; text/image/video -> URDF with actor-critic self-correction). Real2Code (ICLR 2025; up to 10 parts via LLM code). ManiTwin (arXiv 2603.16866; 100K assets with VLM-estimated OBB, mass, friction). SLAT-Phys (2603.23973; material property fields from single image). Phys2Real (2510.11689; VLM priors + online adaptation).
options.license_and_cost: CoACD MIT. V-HACD BSD (from prior knowledge; low confidence). Articulate-Anything MIT. PhysX-Anything S-Lab License (restrictive, non-commercial-style). Others vary.
strengths: Every stage of image->URDF/USD-physics now has a working research method
CoACD emits fewer hulls (typically 4-24 vs V-HACD 10-64), so simulation runs faster
weaknesses: CoACD inflates collision geometry (floating objects when stacked) and is 10-100x slower than V-HACD on CPU
VLM physical priors are coarse; articulation inference fails on unusual mechanisms
PhysX-Anything license blocks direct commercial use
options.best_fit: Backbone of CEN's 'sim-ready certification' stage: re-implement/fine-tune on own data with permissive bases

options.name: Physically based materials: MDL, MaterialX 1.39.x, OpenPBR 1.0, UE Substrate
options.status_as_of_2026: OpenPBR 1.0 (ASWF, Adobe+Autodesk; reference implementation inside MaterialX). MaterialX 1.39.2 (Jan 21, 2025; validated with OpenUSD 25.02). Isaac Sim 6.0 adds MaterialX support; MDL is native to Omniverse RTX; UE 5.7 Substrate production-ready.
options.license_and_cost: Apache-2.0 (MaterialX/OpenPBR); MDL SDK open (BSD-3, prior knowledge; medium confidence).
strengths: Portable PBR across Omniverse, Blender, UE and USD
Measured-material workflows possible
weaknesses: Generative 3D outputs only basic metallic-roughness and need upgrading
Spectral/sensor-band (NIR lidar/radar) material properties are not covered by OpenPBR
options.best_fit: Make OpenPBR/MaterialX the CEN marketplace canonical material, with MDL for RTX and per-band sensor material tables added

options.name: Sensor models: Isaac Sim RTX sensors, camera ISP (PPISP), event cameras (v2e/ESIM/EVIS), tactile (TacSL, Taccel, DIGIT sim)
options.status_as_of_2026: Isaac Sim 6.x isaacsim.sensors.experimental.rtx: OmniLidar, OmniRadar, Acoustic/ultrasonic, camera (docs Jun 22, 2026). Physically-plausible ISP in 3DGRUT (Jan 2026), gsplat (Jul 2026) and Isaac Lab 3.0. key_facts.claim: Isaac Sim 6.0 (GA June 2026) supports 3D Gaussian Splatting via Fabric Scene Delegate with multi-GPU rendering, light interaction with mesh scenes, and MaterialX; splat export moved to the OpenUSD ParticleField3DGaussianSplat schema (.usdc default, .usdz opt-in).
Isaac Sim 6.1.0 GA and 7.0.0a1 pre-release tags exist (Sep 10 and Sep 18); the fetch tool printed the tag years inconsistently, but the 2026 timing follows from 6.0 GA in June 2026.
Isaac Sim recommended datacenter GPUs are A40 (min), L40S (recommended), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server (best). These are RT-core GPUs; H100/A100 are not listed.
OpenUSD 26.03 adds a native UsdVolParticleField schema family, including UsdVolParticleField3DGaussianSplat.
Khronos released KHR_gaussian_splatting as a Release Candidate on Feb 3, 2026 (ratification targeted Q2 2026); Cesium, Babylon.js and PlayCanvas ship support.

3DGRUT is Apache-2.0; v1.1.0 (Jun 10, 2026) added USD/USDZ/PLY/NuRec export with mesh injection; v2.0.0 (Jun 2026) added Neural Harmonic Textures; PPISP (physically-plausible ISP) added Jan 2026; supports fisheye and rolling shutter.
gsplat is Apache-2.0, v1.6.0 on main, with 3DGUT, spinning-lidar rasterization (Mar 2026), NCore v4 (Apr 2026), fisheye/FTheta/lidar camera models (Jun 2026), multi-GPU and PPISP (Jul 2026).

The original Inria 3DGS code (Gaussian-Splatting License) is research/evaluation only; commercial use requires Inria consent. 2DGS and MILo use this license; PGSR's license allows 'educational, research and non-profit purposes only'.
Instant-NGP is under Nvidia Source Code License-NC (non-commercial); nvdiffrast is under Nvidia Source Code License (1-Way Commercial), usable non-commercially only except by NVIDIA.

Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.1 Community License excludes the EU, UK and South Korea from its Territory and forbids use of the Works or their outputs outside the Territory; it also has a >1M MAU approval clause.

TRELLIS.2-4B is MIT-licensed, outputs GLB with PBR (base color, roughness, metallic, opacity), needs ≥24 GB VRAM, and generates 512³/1024³/1536³ in ~3/17/60 s on H100; it depends on nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec with separate licenses.
SAM 3D Objects released Nov 19, 2025 under the SAM License; outputs Gaussian splats (.ply) and pose/layout; encoder weights released Jun 1, 2026.
VGGT-1B-Commercial (Jul 29, 2025) is licensed for commercial use (no military); the original VGGT-1B checkpoint is non-commercial; VGGT-Omega released May 18, 2026.
Depth Anything 3 (Nov 14, 2025): Small/Base/Metric-Large/Mono-Large under Apache-2.0; Large/Giant/Nested-Giant under CC-BY-NC-4.0.
MapAnything code is Apache-2.0; weights come in a CC-BY-NC default and an Apache-2.0 'map-anything-apache' variant.

Cosmos-Transfer2.5 and Predict2.5 released Oct 6, 2025; Transfer controls are depth, edge, blur and segmentation with AV multiview and robot multiview variants; a distilled edge model was released Feb 23, 2026; weights are under the NVIDIA Open Model License (commercial use allowed).
The Cosmos-Predict2.5 repo now receives only limited maintenance; development moved to Cosmos 3 at github.com/NVIDIA/Cosmos.
Cosmos 3 is released under OpenMDW-1.1 (permissive, covers weights, no output restrictions); GitHub lists Super 64B, Nano 16B, Edge 4B (Edge released Jul 2026), while press reported 32B/8B.

At GTC 2026 (Mar 17) NVIDIA introduced Newton 1.0 (open source; co-developed with Google DeepMind and Disney Research), Isaac Lab 3.0 early access and GR00T N1.7 early access with commercial licensing.
Isaac Lab 3.0 offers Isaac RTX, OVRTX (kit-less), Newton Warp, Newton GL and experimental Newton RTX renderers plus a renderer-neutral physically plausible ISP.
AlpaSim is Apache-2.0 (Oct 2025), uses NuRec (3DGUT) as default renderer with OmniDreams video-model rendering as an alternative, and ships about 900 reconstructed 20-second long-tail scenes.
Unreal Engine 5.8 released Jun 17, 2026 with Lumen Lite and MegaLights production-ready; it is the last UE5 release, and UE6 early access is targeted for late 2027.
Unity's 2026 strategy puts HDRP in maintenance (no new features) and prioritizes URP.
WebGPU is on by default in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari 26 (Sep 2025, incl. iOS).
Genie 3 is not available as a developer API; Project Genie (Genie 3 + Nano Banana Pro + Gemini) is a research prototype for US Google AI Ultra subscribers with 60-second sessions.
Wayve GAIA-3 (Dec 2, 2025) is a 15B latent-diffusion multi-camera world model for AV evaluation; GAIA-4 (Aug 3, 2026) is closed-loop and generates radar alongside cameras.

PhysX-Anything (CVPR 2026) generates sim-ready URDF/MJCF with geometry, articulation, mass and friction from a single image using Qwen2.5-VL, but uses the restrictive S-Lab License and deformables are unstable in MuJoCo.
CoACD is MIT-licensed; GPU CuACD (Sep 2026) is ~100x faster (~0.25 s/mesh on RTX 4090).
CoACD tends to inflate collision geometry (visual meshes float when stacked) and is 1-2 orders of magnitude slower than V-HACD.
FID often does not predict detector mAP; SDQM reaches Pearson 0.8719 with YOLOv11n mAP50 and SADGE reaches Pearson 0.88 / Spearman 0.77 with downstream transfer.
TacSL simulates visuotactile images and force fields >200x faster than prior SOTA and is integrated into Isaac Lab (PhysX backend only).
Taccel (NeurIPS 2025, MIT) uses IPC + Affine Body Dynamics to reach 915 FPS total with 4096 parallel environments for vision-based tactile sensors.
World Labs Marble exports splats (SPZ/PLY) plus collider and HQ GLB meshes; GA Nov 12, 2025; World API Jan 2026; Marble 1.1 Apr 2026; commercial rights need the Pro plan.
Decart launched Oasis 3 (Jun 10, 2026), a real-time photoreal driving world model via API at $0.02/s, after a $300M Series C (May 2026, ~$4B valuation).
Event camera simulation is not native in Isaac Sim; EVIS (arXiv 2607.08098, Jul 2026) adds real-time event simulation there, while CARLA has native DVS.
fVDB Reality Capture (Apache-2.0, NVIDIA/OpenVDB) claims ~50% better end-to-end training throughput than gsplat and exports meshes/USD.

recommendations_for_aichemist: Engine decision for realism: adopt, don't build. Use Omniverse RTX via Isaac Sim 6.1+ and Isaac Lab 3.0 as the physically based render + sensor runtime. Use Blender Cycles for offline ground-truth renders on non-RT GPUs. Use the PlayCanvas engine / Spark (MIT, WebGPU/WebGL2) for CEN browser previews. Keep UE 5.8/CARLA as an optional AV connector only. Skip Unity HDRP (frozen) and Godot for realism.

Adopt a 4-layer realism architecture in one OpenUSD stage. (L1) Physics-grounded meshes with MDL/MaterialX/OpenPBR and physics schemas. (L2) Neural-reconstructed backgrounds as UsdVolParticleField3DGaussianSplat (NuRec/3DGUT), with hidden proxy meshes for collision. (L3) Calibrated sensor models: RTX camera + PPISP, lidar, radar, ultrasonic, IMU noise; event via v2e/EVIS; tactile via TacSL/Taccel. (L4) Optional generative post-render augmentation (Cosmos Transfer 2.5 now, Cosmos 3 Nano fine-tuned later) driven by depth/segmentation/edge controls, with automatic label-consistency checks so labels stay valid.

Evolve CEN's NeRF photo->3D pipeline into a 'CEN Real2Sim Forge'. Step 1: capture (phone/robot video, optional lidar). Step 2: feed-forward poses and metric depth (VGGT-1B-Commercial, MapAnything-apache, DA3-Metric-Large Apache). Step 3: 3DGUT splat training on gsplat/3DGRUT (Apache) for the visual layer. Step 4: surface mesh via gsplat-2DGS/fVDB plus an in-house PGSR/MILo-style re-implementation. Step 5: generative completion of unseen parts with TRELLIS.2 (replace nvdiffrast) and SAM 3D Objects for single-view clutter. Step 6: part segmentation + articulation (Articulate-Anything MIT as baseline; in-house model fine-tuned on CEN synthetic articulated data). Step 7: CoACD/CuACD collision. Step 8: VLM priors for mass/friction/material, refined by short interaction videos (system identification). Step 9: automated physics QA (drop, stack, push, joint-limit tests in Newton/PhysX). Step 10: export SimReady USD + URDF/MJCF + glTF (KHR_gaussian_splatting) with a 'sim-ready certificate' score.

Make the moat data plus validation, not models. Monetize (a) certified sim-ready assets and (b) captured Korean environments: factories, logistics centers, shipyards, retail, Korean roads and signage, BIM-aligned sites. Also sell (c) paired real/sim datasets with measured gap scores. Feed customer captures back to fine-tune the generative/articulation models under clear data-rights terms.

Run an immediate license audit (weeks, not months). Identify what CEN's current NeRF uses: Instant-NGP is NC; nerfstudio is Apache. Remove all Inria-derived 3DGS code (2DGS, SuGaR, MILo, PGSR, original 3DGS rasterizer, TRELLIS v1 diffoctreerast), nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec, CC-BY-NC weights and Hunyuan3D 2.x (license excludes South Korea). Standardize on Apache/MIT/OpenMDW components and get NVIDIA written confirmation on Omniverse/NuRec use in a multi-tenant cloud SaaS.

Ship a Sim2Real Gap Scorecard as a first-class CEN feature. Rendering: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on held-out views. Perception: mAP_real of a synth-trained model divided by mAP_real of a real-trained one, few-shot real fine-tune curves, plus SDQM/SADGE-style predictors; FID/KID/CMMD as secondary only. Policy: paired sim-vs-real success over ≥5 policies, reporting Pearson r and ranking agreement, following PolaRiS. Physics: trajectory ADE/FDE, rest-pose error, contact force error. Sensors: lidar range/intensity error, Chamfer distance, noise PSD.

Domain strategy: use Real2Sim splats to remove the target-site gap; structured domain randomization (Replicator) for the long tail; generative domain adaptation (Cosmos Transfer) for appearance diversity only; and always a small real fine-tune. Prioritize by measured scorecard gain per GPU-hour.

GPU plan: split the CEN cloud into an RT-core render pool (L40S / RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell; Isaac Sim min A40) and a training/generative pool (H100/H200/B200 for gsplat training, TRELLIS.2, Cosmos). Budget estimate (my estimate, not sourced): 16-32 RT-core GPUs plus 8-16 H100-class for the first 12 months of the realism workstream.

Team for this workstream (estimate): 2-3 neural reconstruction (3DGS/3DGUT, lidar splats); 2 geometry/sim-ready (meshing, CoACD, USD physics); 2 generative 3D (TRELLIS.2 fine-tune, articulation, physical-property VLM); 1-2 sensor modeling (camera ISP, lidar/radar, tactile); 2 world-model post-training (Cosmos Transfer/Cosmos 3); 1-2 evaluation/metrics + real-data capture ops; 1 technical artist/material (OpenPBR/MDL). About 11-14 FTE.

Roadmap. Q4 2026: license audit; NeRF->3DGUT migration; Isaac Sim 6.1 NuRec import/export; WebGPU splat viewer in the marketplace. Q1-Q2 2027: rigid-object Forge v1 (mesh + collision + VLM mass/friction + physics QA), scene-scale capture for 2-3 Korean pilot sites, scorecard v1. Q3 2027: articulation + sensor profiles (lidar/radar/event) + Cosmos Transfer augmentation with label QA. Q4 2027-2028: deformables (PhysTwin-style), world-model-based policy evaluation (Cosmos 3), relightable splats; track the UE6 and Cosmos 3.x transitions.

Track and benchmark quarterly, but do not build on: Genie 3 (no API), GAIA-3/4 (proprietary), Decart Oasis 3 and Runway GWM-1 (APIs could be optional long-tail video sources), World Labs Marble (possible environment API partner and also a competitor), Hunyuan3D 3.x (API only; Korea terms unverified).
risks: License contamination. Most high-quality 3DGS mesh-extraction code (2DGS, MILo, PGSR, SuGaR?) and NVIDIA research code (Instant-NGP, nvdiffrast, Neuralangelo) are non-commercial. Hunyuan3D 2.1 explicitly bans use in South Korea. Shipping any of these in CEN creates IP liability and could block enterprise sales or M&A.

NVIDIA lock-in. Omniverse license terms for multi-tenant cloud SaaS, the RT-core GPU requirement (H100 fleets cannot run RTX rendering efficiently) and rapid API churn (sensors.rtx deprecated in 6.0; Cosmos 2.5 superseded in ~8 months) raise switching costs.

Splat limitations. Lighting is baked unless relightable variants are used. Splats have no inherent physics or collision, so proxy meshes are needed. Novel-view extrapolation away from capture trajectories degrades, and lidar/radar on splats is less mature than on meshes, so the sensor gap can persist even when RGB looks perfect.

Generative 3D outputs are not simulation-truthful: they lack metric scale, contain hallucinated hidden geometry, are non-watertight and have no physical parameters. VLM-estimated mass/friction can be off by large factors, so policies trained on them may fail on contact-rich tasks without system-ID refinement.

Generative world models (Cosmos, GAIA, Genie, Decart) can hallucinate physics and shift object boundaries. That silently corrupts labels in synthetic datasets, and they are costly per frame. Overreliance undermines CEN's 'controllable, reproducible' value proposition.
Metric risk: FID/KID can look good while detector mAP or policy success does not transfer. Without paired real data the platform cannot prove realism claims to customers.

Competitive risk: NVIDIA (NuRec, Cosmos, SimReady), World Labs (Marble splat+collider worlds) and Meshy/Tripo/Rodin are moving into sim-ready asset/world generation, so a pure 'photo->3D' feature will be commoditized within 12-18 months.

Privacy and regulatory risk when capturing real Korean sites and roads (faces, license plates, factory IP) under PIPA and customer NDAs. Capture pipelines need anonymization (blurring/inpainting) before splat training and marketplace distribution.
Engine transition risk: UE6 early access in late 2027 and Unity HDRP stagnation make game-engine-centric investments short-lived.
Research-to-product risk: many key methods (PhysTwin, PolaRiS, PhysX-Anything, Articulate-Anything) are single-paper codebases with limited robustness and maintenance.
